question.problem:
$$

Given that $p\ge 25,$ express $\operatorname{arcosh}⁡(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p})$ using the definition of the inverse hyperbolic cosine.

$\operatorname{arcosh}⁡(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p})=\operatorname{ln}⁡($
{{field-1}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
The definition of $\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x$ is 

$$
\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arcosh}⁡(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p}+\sqrt{{(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p})}^{2}-1}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p}+\sqrt{\frac{{p}^{4}+50{p}^{2}+625}{100{p}^{2}}-1}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p}+\sqrt{\frac{{p}^{4}-50{p}^{2}+625}{100{p}^{2}}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p}+\sqrt{{(\frac{{p}^{2}-25}{10p})}^{2}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p}+|\frac{{p}^{2}-25}{10p}|)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $p\ge 25,$ we have $\frac{{p}^{2}-25}{10p}>0,$ and we can remove the absolute value in the above expression. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arcosh}⁡(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{p}^{2}+25}{10p}+\frac{{p}^{2}-25}{10p}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{p}{5}).\end{aligned}
$$
